step1.title: Install and sign in to Tailscale (this computer and your phone)
step1.body: Install Tailscale on both devices and sign in with the same account; your phone then reaches this computer at a 100.x.x.x address from anywhere.
step1.sameAccount: Sign in on both with the same account (Google, Apple, GitHub…) and turn Connect on.

step2.title: Create a device token
step2.body: The key your phone uses to get in. Make one per device; if one is lost, revoke just that one. The value is shown once, when it is created.
step2.confirmRevoke: Revoke the '{{name}}' token? Devices using it are cut off immediately.
step2.qrHint: Once remote access is on, scan this with your phone camera to sign in without typing the token. Keep it out of sight of others.
step2.onceWarning: This value is shown only now. After you confirm it cannot be shown again — copy it if you need it.

step3.title: Turn on remote access
step3.body: With remote access on, only devices with a token get in, and only to the allowed features (viewing and creating tickets, …).
step3.roots: Folders tickets from your phone may run in
step3.rootsHint: Remote tickets only run inside these folders. The wider they are, the more a leaked token can do.
step3.bind_allHint: This computer uses localhost, your phone the Tailscale address. The port is visible on the same Wi-Fi too, but useless without a token.
step3.bind_tailscaleHint: Reachable only over Tailscale. This computer must also use the Tailscale address instead of localhost, and the server will not start while Tailscale is off.
step3.terminal_watch: Watch — read sessions, conversations, terminal output
step3.terminal_shell: Shell — also open and close terminals
step3.terminalRisk_watch: A leaked token lets someone read your code and prompts.
step3.terminalRisk_input: A leaked token lets someone run commands on this computer.
step3.terminalRisk_shell: A leaked token gives someone a shell on this computer.

step4.title: Open it on your phone
step4.needRemote: Turn remote access on in step 3 and restart the server; the address appears here.
step4.needTailscale: The address appears once Tailscale is connected on this computer (step 1).
step4.s1: Open the Tailscale app on your phone and turn Connect on.
step4.s2: Scan the QR with the camera, or type the address in the browser.
step4.s3: When asked for a token, paste the one from step 2. (Automatic if you opened the token QR.)
step4.s4: Use 'Add to Home Screen' in the browser menu to keep it like an app.
step4.useTailscaleAddress: Always open the Tailscale address starting with 100.x. Opening the Wi-Fi IP sends the token unencrypted.

cause.exited: The agent exited with an error

meaning.terminated: The agent did not crash. Something outside it asked it to stop, and it shut itself down mid-run. The work up to that point was done and paid for — this is not a verdict on the work.
meaning.interrupted: An interrupt (Ctrl-C, or a parent shell) reached the agent process and it stopped.
meaning.hangup: The terminal or parent process the agent was attached to disappeared, so the OS hung the agent up.
meaning.killed: The agent was killed outright with no chance to shut down or save anything. On macOS this is almost always memory pressure or an explicit kill -9.
meaning.spawn-failed: No process ever ran: there is no exit status at all. This is an environment problem, not an agent problem.
meaning.exited: The agent process ran and ended itself with a non-zero status. The reason is usually in its error output below.
meaning.no-result: The process exited cleanly but never streamed a usable final answer, so there was nothing to verify.

suspect.cancel: A cancel request for this ticket (from the dashboard or the phone app)
suspect.serverStop: The open-alive server was stopped or restarted
suspect.otherTool: Another tool or script on this machine cleaning up processes
suspect.ctrlC: Ctrl-C in the terminal that started the server
suspect.processGroup: An interrupt delivered to the server's whole process group
suspect.terminalClosed: The terminal that started the server was closed
suspect.sshDropped: An SSH session carrying the run dropped
suspect.supervisor: A container or supervisor forcing the process down
suspect.notOnPath: The `claude` binary is not on the server's PATH
suspect.cwdUnreadable: The working directory is missing or unreadable
suspect.sshUnreachable: For a remote run, the SSH host could not be reached
suspect.usageError: A bad CLI flag or argument
suspect.authOrQuota: Expired auth or a usage limit
suspect.agentError: An error inside the agent — read the error output below
suspect.maxTurns: The run hit its maximum number of turns
suspect.streamCutOff: The output stream ended before the result event

next.terminated: Retry the ticket — nothing about the work failed.
next.interrupted: Start the server detached so an interrupt cannot reach the agents, then retry.
next.hangup: Run the server in the background (open-alive start) and retry.
next.killed: Check memory use and lower the number of tickets running at once, then retry.
next.spawn-failed: Fix the environment first — confirm the server can find `claude` and reach the working directory.
next.exited: Read the error output below before retrying.
next.no-result: Narrow the goal or split it into rounds, then retry.
